title: A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree
summary: An integer polynomial is intersective if it has a root modulo every positive integer. For each degree k ≥ 2, we prove that there is an exponent $`c_k\gt 0`$ such that every set $`A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}`$ whose differences avoid all nonzero values $`h(1),h(2),\ldots`$, where h is an intersective polynomial of degree k with positive leading coefficient, satisfies $`|A|=O_h(N^{1-c_k})`$. The implied constant may depend on h , but the power-saving exponent depends only on its degree.
family_title: Power savings for intersective polynomial differences and prime arguments

review.reason: Proves power-saving bounds for sets avoiding differences given by intersective polynomials.
